\section{Introduction}
A diffusion language model can buy sequential computation twice. It \emph{owns} depth:
$d$ transformer blocks, paid once in parameters and then on every forward pass forever.
It \emph{rents} refinement steps: $T$ denoising passes over the same sequence, paid per
utterance and adjustable at serve time. An autoregressive model has only the first lever;
its serial cost per token is fixed by the architecture the moment training ends. If rented
serial compute substitutes for owned serial compute, a deployment can trade parameters for
steps after the fact --- but only for the capabilities that steps actually improve.

Zero-shot text-to-speech is an unusually clean probe of that question, because it separates
two capabilities that are measured by standard, independent metrics. Intelligibility is
compositional: the model must place the right phonetic content in the right order, and word
error rate (WER) reads it out. Speaker identity is representational: the model must carry
timbre from a short prompt into new content, and speaker similarity (SIM-o) reads that out.
The two need not respond to the same knob.

We train one iso-parameter width--depth grid of masked-diffusion codec language models and
then sweep $T$ at inference only, which yields a full $(w, d, T)$ response surface per
metric at zero additional training cost. Two claims were pre-registered before any run.
\textbf{H-D2}: refinement steps improve intelligibility more than identity, i.e.\ test-time
scaling is metric-selective. \textbf{H-D3}: for intelligibility, steps and depth exchange at
a measurable rate $\kappa$ --- how many step-doublings buy one depth-doubling.

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:models}
\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m d^{-\beta_m} + C_m T^{-\tau_m}
\qquad
\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m \big(d\,T^{\kappa_m}\big)^{-\beta_m}
\end{equation}

[INTRO PARA 3 + CONTRIBUTIONS: Phase 7, with \Ndtau/\Ndtauci and \Nkappawer/\Nkappawerci.]

\section{Related work}
Masked diffusion language models are now trained at scale \citep{llada,mdlm,d3pm}, but their
scaling is reported against a single likelihood-shaped objective, so a per-capability
question cannot arise. In speech, the masked-generative recipes that made codec-token TTS
practical --- confidence-decoded parallel generation over residual codebook levels
\citep{soundstorm,maskgit} and its multi-stage successors \citep{maskgct} --- fixed a step
budget by engineering judgement and reported a single operating point; none maps error
against steps as a law. Autoregressive codec TTS \citep{valle} has begun to report scaling
behaviour, but in total parameters $N$ only \citep{llasa}, which cannot separate width from
depth and has no step axis at all; classical scaling work is likewise $N$-indexed
\citep{kaplan,chinchilla}. Test-time scaling is well studied in reasoning
\citep{testtime}, where the payoff is measured on one correctness metric; whether extra
inference compute helps different capabilities \emph{differently} is, to our knowledge,
untested in generative speech. That is the gap this abstract fills: per-metric laws in
$(w, d, T)$ for a masked-diffusion TTS model.

\section{Method}
\paragraph{Backbone and objective.}
A bidirectional (non-causal) pre-LN transformer over Mimi \citep{moshi} codec tokens at 12.5\,Hz with the
first 8 residual codebooks (2048 entries each, plus MASK and PAD). Width $w$, depth $d$,
head dimension 64, GELU MLP ratio 4, RMSNorm, RoPE, no weight tying, so the non-embedding
parameter count is $N = 12\,d\,w^{2}$. One embedding table per codebook is summed at the
input and one linear head per codebook reads out. Training is SoundStorm-style \citep{soundstorm}
coarse-to-fine masking: per example a level $l \sim \mathcal{U}\{1..8\}$ and a ratio
$t \sim \mathcal{U}(0,1]$; levels below $l$ stay visible, level $l$ is masked i.i.d.\ with
probability $t$, levels above $l$ are entirely MASK; the loss is cross-entropy on the masked
cells of level $l$ only. A phoneme prefix and a 3-second prompt of codec tokens are always
visible; there is no speaker encoder, so the backbone itself is the only identity pathway,
and no classifier-free guidance, which would add a second inference-time axis and confound
the step axis. The target length is fixed before generation from the text length and a
corpus character rate ($\Nsecperchar$\,s/char).

\paragraph{Frozen sampler.}
MaskGIT-style confidence decoding \citep{maskgit}, level by level, with exactly $T$ refinement steps per level, so
NFE $= 8T$: a cosine schedule sets how many cells remain masked after each step, tokens are
drawn categorically at temperature 1.0, and confidences are log-probabilities plus Gumbel
noise annealed $1 \to 0$ within a level; committed cells stay committed. The sampler is
identical for every config, seed and $T$ --- nothing is tuned per shape or per step budget.
Per-item generation noise is keyed so that each item sees the same noise at the first step of
every level for every $T$, making $T$ the only difference between surface points of one run.
Before any metric is computed we verify that $T$ reaches the sampler: outputs at $T{=}1$ and
$T{=}16$ must differ on more than 20\% of generated token cells.

\paragraph{Design and statistics.}
$\Nconfigs$ configs span three iso-$N$ budgets $\times$ five aspect ratios, each trained at
$\Nseeds$ seeds for 30{,}000 steps at effective batch 256 with $\mu$P \citep{mup} (base width 256, base
LR $\Nbaselr$); width transfer and depth transfer were verified by five-point LR sweeps
before the grid. $T \in \{\NTgrid\}$ is swept at evaluation only, giving $\Nsurface$ surface
points per metric from $\Nruns$ trained models. Metrics: WER (Whisper-large-v3 \citep{whisper}, greedy, the
Whisper English normaliser), SIM-o (WavLM-large \citep{wavlm} speaker-verification embedding against the
\emph{original} prompt waveform, following \citet{seedtts}), a frozen degenerate-output rule, and UTMOS \citep{utmos} as a tertiary.
Error transforms are $\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{WER}} = \mathrm{WER}$ and
$\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{SIM}} = 1 - \text{SIM-o}$, computed over all items including
degenerates. Both forms of Eq.~\eqref{eq:models} are fitted by weighted non-linear least
squares with 32 multi-starts; $\Delta\tau = \tau_{\mathrm{WER}} - \tau_{\mathrm{SIM}}$,
$\kappa$, and $\Delta\rho = \alpha_{\mathrm{SIM}}/\beta_{\mathrm{SIM}} -
\alpha_{\mathrm{WER}}/\beta_{\mathrm{WER}}$ carry percentile confidence intervals from a
bootstrap that resamples at the \emph{run} level --- the five $T$-points of one run share a
trained model, so resampling surface points would understate their correlation --- with
$\Nbootreps$ replicates recomputing every $T$ point.

\section{Limitations and outlook}
[LIMITATIONS: Phase 7 — scale ceiling, single language, single codec, CFG excluded, any
calendar cuts (\Ncuts), outcome-class caveats.]

\paragraph{Reproducibility.}
The protocol, hypotheses, thresholds, frozen sampler and analysis plan were registered
before the first training run; the released artefact contains the harness, every run record,
the full surface, and the fitting and bootstrap code. Data is a $\Nhours$\,h English subset
of a public corpus \citep{emilia} with $\Nspeakers$ speakers and 200 speakers held out; total cost
$\Ngpuhours$ GPU-hours.
